Resolves #20184

A long-form post, `learn/blog/a-data-grid-in-a-web-worker.md`, titled *The main thread is the wrong place for a data grid* and registered in the portal blog. It is written for a stranger who knows neither Neo.mjs nor multi-threading and decides from the preview alone. The title is a claim the reader may disagree with. The story explains workers from zero, the benchmarks repository is the reference throughout, and DevIndex is the real app. The arc:

1. the reader's freeze (the report's 329 ms);
2. the main thread and long tasks;
3. why virtualization, one-off worker offloading and server-side data leave the work in place;
4. web workers, with the App Worker as the main actor;
5. five grid decisions read from source, and what the pool means for accessibility, column drag and cell editing;
6. the benchmark, wins and losses;
7. DevIndex;
8. the table and the grid from 2019, the grid's restart in December 2024, and on to 13.3;
9. the grid's limits;
10. where to try it.

The image dependency neomjs/pages#60 is merged; the DevIndex image serves 200.

Evidence: L1 (docs; the registry parses; links checked; every capability read at source on `dev` or measured on the production examples) → L1 required (no runtime ACs). Residual: AC-4 (post-publish Medium URL and ledger row), Residual-Owner: #19575.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the baseline `pr-body` and `substrate-size` checks run in CI. Change class: zero-delta (`docs`).

## Deltas from ticket
- The title is Fix0's contrarian candidate in statement form: r/javascript sends question posts to its Ask flair, and a statement reads the same in every venue the post reaches.
- DevIndex is the lead image and the cover: a real app at 50,000 rows says more than the synthetic bigData table, which looks plain.
- Public links use the production builds: the dev-mode `/examples/` URLs rendered blank or unstyled in headless Chromium.
- This PR also fixes two links in `building-a-multi-window-dashboard-with-dock-layouts.md`. They pointed at `/news/blog/blog/<slug>`, which 404s; the static route is `/news/blog/<slug>`. Maryam found the shape in this post's own publish request.

## Test Evidence
- **Link check:** every URL `curl -sL` → 200, including those added on 31 Oct (#6169, #6172, the W3C APG grid pattern, `SortZone.mjs`, `grid/column/Component.mjs` and the corrected dock-layouts link). The post's own static route serves after deploy.
- **Source reads on `dev`:**
  - `src/grid/Body.mjs`: the row pool, fixed DOM order through `translate3d`, `bufferRowRange` 3, `bufferColumnRange`.
  - `src/grid/Row.mjs`, added 2026-02-03 (#8965).
  - `Store#autoInitRecords`, `src/data/parser/Stream.mjs` (chunked NDJSON) and `src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs`.
  - `src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs`: the proxy is a small grid built from the header and one cell per visible row; live component cells move into it via `moveNode` and come back on drop.
  - `src/grid/column/Component.mjs`: one component per pool slot.
  - The table: sticky `th` and docked `neo-locked` columns since 2019.
  - DevIndex `GridContainer`: 37 columns, one per year since 2010. Its username field is a store filter, so the walkthrough switches the data mode first.
- **Measured on neomjs.com production (31 Oct):**
  - bigData: `aria-rowcount` 20,001; scrolled to the middle, its 32 DOM rows carry `aria-rowindex` 9,997–10,028.
  - A MutationObserver counted 0 elements added or removed over 3,000 px and 30,000 px of scrolling; text and attribute changes only.
  - ArrowDown moves the row selection after one round trip.
  - The issues showcase numbered its locked regions separately (#20187). #20189 fixed it on `dev`, merged before this PR, so the release that publishes the post ships the fix to the live showcase.
- **Benchmark arithmetic:** each per-jump time is a scroll total ÷ 8 (Neo.mjs 29.2–47.4 ms, AG Grid 16.0–16.8 ms). The small-update and filter gaps come from the report's total-time tables (5.26–53.18 ms).
- **Not run:** a portal render of the route (see Post-Merge Validation).

     - **What actually happens in the code:** Typing into **Username** (`name: 'login'` in `devindex` `ControlsContainer.mjs:61-69`) invokes `MainContainerController#onFilterChange` (`L104-121`) → `Collection#filter()` (`src/collection/Base.mjs:941-962`), which filters `store._items` down to the matching subset (typically **1 developer**), moving the 50,000 unfiltered records into `store.allItems`. Because `this._items` holds only the filtered projection (`length === 1`), **switching Data Mode while filtered to a username only sorts that 1 filtered row, NOT all 50,000 developers** — and visually the reader only sees their single row stay in place with its cell values changing, rather than seeing the 50,000-row leaderboard re-rank!
